Hailing from Lafayette, Louisiana, and rooted deep in Cajun culture, Troy Richard serves up his own unique blend of musical gumbo. Bringing together a rich mix of sounds, influences, and Louisiana flavor, Troy delivers a solo performance that is as authentic and soulful as the roots he comes from.

events.title: Roddie Romero and The Hub City Allstars
events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.desc:
Straight out of the heart of Acadiana, Roddie Romero & The Hub City Allstars bring the unmistakable sound and spirit of South Louisiana to the stage. Blending traditional Cajun and Creole music with zydeco, swamp pop, blues, funk, soul, and rock 'n' roll, this powerhouse Louisiana band delivers a sound that is as deeply rooted as it is refreshingly original.

Led by singer, songwriter, accordionist, and slide guitarist Roddie Romero, the band celebrates the rich musical heritage of Louisiana while pushing its boundaries into exciting new territory. With soulful vocals, fiery accordion, masterful guitar work, and infectious rhythms, their music captures everything that makes South Louisiana special.

A three-time Grammy-nominated group, the Hub City Allstars have spent more than two decades performing at prestigious festivals and venues, earning recognition for their musicianship, original songwriting, and electrifying live performances. Their critically acclaimed albums, including The La Louisianne Sessions and Gulfstream , showcase a band equally comfortable honoring Louisiana's musical traditions and creating something entirely their own.

events.title: $ideQue$t
events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.desc:
SideQuest LA

Two powerhouse Louisiana musicians, one shared love of great music. SideQuest LA brings together vocalist, songwriter, and drummer Gino V. and guitarist, vocalist, and songwriter Zach Edwards for a musical collaboration that refuses to stay in one lane.

Rooted in the sounds of South Louisiana but reaching well beyond its musical borders, SideQuest blends soul, blues, R&B, funk, hip-hop, and good old-fashioned rock and roll. The duo combines original songwriting with unexpected takes on some of their favorite songs, creating a show that is as versatile as it is entertaining.

Gino V., born and raised in Delcambre, Louisiana, is a seasoned musician known for his commanding vocals, deep grooves, and dynamic musicianship. He has performed with some of Acadiana's respected artists and notably played drums for Louisiana music legend Wayne Toups.

Zach Edwards adds his own distinctive guitar work, vocals, and songwriting to the mix, bringing together the blues, rock, and roots influences that make the SideQuest sound uniquely their own.

Whether delivering soulful originals, stretching out on a blues-rock groove, or putting their own spin on familiar favorites, SideQuest LA brings plenty of musical firepower and personality to the stage.

Expect big grooves, soulful vocals, killer guitar work, and a little bit of everything. SideQuest is anything but an ordinary night of live music.

events.title: Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market
events.desc: Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market Every Saturday | 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM | Moncus Park | Rain or Shine There is no better way to start a Saturday in Acadiana. Every week, the Lafayette Farmers and Artisans Market transforms the heart of Moncus Park into a lively gathering place, where local farmers, artisans, and craftspeople come together to share the best of our region. Wander the rows and you will find tables overflowing with just-picked produce, local honey, fresh flowers, baked goods, handmade crafts, and one-of-a-kind finds from the makers who pour their hearts into them. Whether you come for the produce, the people, or simply the joy of a morning outdoors, the market is where Lafayette starts its weekend. Come hungry, shop local, and make a morning of it! Parking & Getting There We guide thousands of visitors in and out every Saturday morning, so parking may take a few extra minutes during peak times, but our team keeps things moving all morning! Our parking lot is $2 per hour, or free for Moncus Park members. All proceeds support Moncus Park, a nonprofit park conservancy. Please only park at Moncus Park, towing is strictly enforced by a third party in neighboring lots. Prefer to skip the parking altogether? Walking or biking in is always a breeze! Weekly Vendor Lineup Curious who's setting up shop this Saturday? Check the Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market Facebook page the Friday before market day for the full vendor list. Become a Vendor Interested in joining us as a farmer, artisan, or maker? The Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market is a producer-only market, meaning all products sold must be grown, raised, baked, crafted, or otherwise produced by the vendor. Reselling products made by someone else is not permitted. Vendor applications are accepted twice each year during the following application periods: January 1 - February 15 July 1 - August 15 The market currently hosts more than 150 vendors, and many categories are at capacity. At this time, we are not accepting applications from most non-farm-based vendors until the next application period. However, we are always interested in hearing from local producers of fresh produce, meat, dairy, and other farm-based products. Before applying, please review our vendor categories and eligibility requirements in the Market Rules & Regulations. Questions can be directed to market@moncuspark.org. If you'd like to learn more, visit the market website: Market at Moncus Park Questions? Reach the market team anytime at market@moncuspark.org. To learn more, visit the market's website: marketatmoncuspark.com

Elise Riley

Carrying on a proud Louisiana musical legacy while bringing her own energy and personality to the stage, Elise Riley is part of a new generation keeping Cajun music alive and moving forward.

Born and raised in Lafayette, Louisiana, Elise grew up surrounded by the sounds and traditions of Cajun music. With legendary Louisiana musician Steve Riley as her father and musician Chris Stafford as her brother, music has always been a central part of her life.

A talented drummer, vocalist, and multi-instrumentalist, Elise has developed her own voice in the South Louisiana music scene. She co-leads Chère Élise, a Lafayette-based Cajun band that brings together traditional Cajun sounds and fresh musical influences. She also performs with Prends Courage, continuing to explore and celebrate the region's rich musical heritage.

Whether behind the drums or stepping forward as a vocalist, Elise brings infectious energy, musicianship, and a genuine appreciation for the music that shaped her.

Rooted in tradition but never afraid to make it her own, Elise Riley represents the next generation of Louisiana musicians carrying Cajun music into the future.

Grand Nathaniel

Hailing from Lafayette, Louisiana, Grand Nathaniel is the musical project of longtime Acadiana musician J. Burton, a fixture in the local music scene for more than three decades.

Blending dreamy lo-fi pop, synth-driven melodies, alternative rock, and nostalgic electronic textures, Grand Nathaniel creates music that feels both familiar and otherworldly. Drawing inspiration from decades of pop, rock, and experimental music, Burton crafts richly layered songs filled with atmosphere, imagination, and a little mystery.

A veteran of the Lafayette music scene, Burton has explored a wide range of sounds through projects including Dire Wood, FIGHTs, Talker, and Grand Nathaniel & the Ghosts. His solo work brings those musical experiences together in a distinctive style he describes as fantasy-pop.

With releases including At the Lagoon and Lonely Wanderer , Grand Nathaniel continues to build an imaginative musical world where nostalgic sounds meet fresh perspectives.

For fans of thoughtful songwriting, atmospheric pop, and adventurous indie music, Grand Nathaniel offers something a little different from the ordinary.

Come experience the sound and imagination of one of Lafayette's longtime independent musical voices.

events.title: Marley's Ghost (West Coast/Cali/Washington)
events.desc:
As most people will tell you, there’s an undeniable connection between versatility and variation. Suffice it to say that each depends on the other. In the case of Seattle-based Marley’s Ghost, that eclectic energy has resulted in a broad repertoire that has defied any ability to tag them to any one particular genre. Their dozen albums to date— like the output of The Band— survey a broad scope of Americana and acoustic music in general, refusing to confine them to any singular niche.
“It is, and always has been, about the music,” bassist, fiddler, guitarist, singer and chief songwriter Dan Wheetman insists. “That’s what’s kept this band going for so long. It’s always been about digging a little deeper, honing our skills and celebrating the entire playing process. That drives us forward.”
With their current album, the aptly named Travelin’ Shoes, Marley’s Ghost veers towards a path that doesn’t detract from that overarched umbrella, but instead helps define it further. Produced by acclaimed virtuoso Larry Campbell (Bob Dylan, Levon Helm), who was previously behind the boards for The Woodstock Sessions, their highly acclaimed 2016 album, Travelin’ Shoes is a joyous and surprisingly diverse set of songs, a celebratory salute to the finest traditions of American music.

events.title: Brass Bed
events.venue: Blue Moon Saloon and Guest House
events.desc:
Brass Bed

Emerging from Lafayette, Louisiana, Brass Bed has spent years carving out a distinctive place in the independent music scene with a sound that blends psychedelic rock, power pop, indie rock, and adventurous songwriting.

Formed in 2004, the band built a reputation for crafting catchy melodies wrapped in swirling guitars, analog synthesizers, fuzz, and expansive psychedelic textures. Drawing inspiration from artists like The Beatles, The Beach Boys, Big Star, and classic alternative rock, Brass Bed balances infectious pop sensibilities with an unpredictable, experimental edge.

The band earned critical acclaim with albums including Melt White (2010), The Secret Will Keep You (2013), and In the Yellow Leaf (2016). Their music has taken them beyond Louisiana, including a memorable appearance on NPR's Tiny Desk Concert series.

Featuring longtime members Jonny Campos, Peter DeHart, and Christiaan Mader, Brass Bed returned with new music in 2025, bringing fresh energy and sharper songwriting to their signature sound.

With deep roots in Acadiana and a sound that reaches far beyond regional boundaries, Brass Bed delivers a live experience full of shimmering melodies, gritty guitars, psychedelic exploration, and good old-fashioned rock and roll.

The best slide guitarists in Minnesota with the notable exception of Leo Kottke. He had opened or played with such greats as Willie Dixon, Albert King, Sonny Landreth, The Hawaiian Slack Key Masters and Geno Delafose and French Rocking Boogie.

events.title: Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market
events.desc: Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market Every Saturday | 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM | Moncus Park | Rain or Shine There is no better way to start a Saturday in Acadiana. Every week, the Lafayette Farmers and Artisans Market transforms the heart of Moncus Park into a lively gathering place, where local farmers, artisans, and craftspeople come together to share the best of our region. Wander the rows and you will find tables overflowing with just-picked produce, local honey, fresh flowers, baked goods, handmade crafts, and one-of-a-kind finds from the makers who pour their hearts into them. Whether you come for the produce, the people, or simply the joy of a morning outdoors, the market is where Lafayette starts its weekend. Come hungry, shop local, and make a morning of it! Parking & Getting There We guide thousands of visitors in and out every Saturday morning, so parking may take a few extra minutes during peak times, but our team keeps things moving all morning! Our parking lot is $2 per hour, or free for Moncus Park members. All proceeds support Moncus Park, a nonprofit park conservancy. Please only park at Moncus Park, towing is strictly enforced by a third party in neighboring lots. Prefer to skip the parking altogether? Walking or biking in is always a breeze! Weekly Vendor Lineup Curious who's setting up shop this Saturday? Check the Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market Facebook page the Friday before market day for the full vendor list. Become a Vendor Interested in joining us as a farmer, artisan, or maker? The Lafayette Farmers & Artisans Market is a producer-only market, meaning all products sold must be grown, raised, baked, crafted, or otherwise produced by the vendor. Reselling products made by someone else is not permitted. Vendor applications are accepted twice each year during the following application periods: January 1 - February 15 July 1 - August 15 The market currently hosts more than 150 vendors, and many categories are at capacity. At this time, we are not accepting applications from most non-farm-based vendors until the next application period. However, we are always interested in hearing from local producers of fresh produce, meat, dairy, and other farm-based products. Before applying, please review our vendor categories and eligibility requirements in the Market Rules & Regulations. Questions can be directed to market@moncuspark.org. events.desc: Join AcA Visual Arts Director Jaik Faulk in conversation with exhibiting artist Kate Gordon. Kate Gordon’s studio practice focuses on painting in the expanded field, sourcing inspiration from pop-up books, dioramas, and collage. The dream imagery that Gordon mines aims to capture the strangeness of the waking world, which is often not as logical as it might at first appear. Gordon has shown her paintings, collages, and video works nationally; exhibitions include a site-specific installation “Alligator Naps” at the Hilliard Art Museum, curation into the Weatherspoon Art Museum’s “Art on Paper” exhibition, and an invitation to create a public video installation at Block 2, a visual platform for new media artists in Raleigh, NC. Most recent professional accomplishments include participation in Kolaj Institute’s Artist Residency in Scotland, curation into “Is This Too Much?”, a maximalist exhibition at Le Mieux Galleries, and inclusion in the “Louisiana Contemporary” exhibition at the Ogden Museum of Southern Art. Gordon currently holds the position of Associate Professor of Figure Drawing & Foundations at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette. She earned an M.F.A. from the University of North Carolina at Greensboro and a B.F.A. from Pratt Institute.

events.title: Ruben Moreno
events.desc:
Ruben Moreno is a musical alchemist whose Zydeco journey began at the tender age of 7, when the rhythmic patter of a washboard first sparked his creative fire. By 10, he was lighting up the stage at Austin’s iconic Continental Club with Leroy Thomas & the Zydeco Roadrunners, setting the tone for a career that blends tradition with innovation.
Mentored by legends like Leroy Thomas, C.J. Chenier, and Andre Thierry, Ruben quickly emerged as the youngest gem in C.J. Chenier’s Red-Hot Louisiana Band. His 2011 debut solo album, Por Ti Volare, produced by Thierry, soared like a phoenix, earning accolades from icons such as Buckwheat Zydeco.
Ever the boundary-breaker, Ruben weaves Zydeco with soulful threads of blues, Chicano grooves, and hip-hop. His creative ventures include a Certified Gold collaboration on Texas Sun with Khruangbin and Leon Bridges, as well as dynamic projects with Baby Bash that bridge the gap between classic Zydeco rhythms and contemporary beats. His latest work showcases that versatility: At the Trailride: Live at Stubb’s has already surpassed 175K streams across platforms, while his single The Recipe (This Heart) has earned more than 1 million streams and continues to grow, spotlighting his ability to craft music that is both deeply authentic and universally relatable.
From enchanting nights at the New Orleans Jazz Fest to electrifying 70,000-strong audiences at Austin City Limits Festival 2024, Ruben’s performances are vibrant canvases where passion meets innovation. With international tours, competition accolades, and congressional recognition for his community contributions, Ruben Moreno continues to light the way—blending the timeless spirit of Zydeco with the pulse of tomorrow.

events.title: The American Creed in Words and Images
events.desc:
For teachers of 6–12 grade
America’s 250th anniversary is an ideal time to reflect on and explore the American Creed, what economist Gunnar Myrdal refers to as “ (what) Americans of all national origins, classes, regions, creeds, and colors, have . . . in common: a social ethos, a political creed.” Since 2018, students around the country have been discussing American Creed videos (streaming on PBS LearningMedia) in class, with curricular support from the National Writing Project. Students have also been invited to create and share their own stories and reflections in photos, captions and/or essays via KQED’s national Youth Media Challenge publishing platform. This workshop supports adding Louisiana voices, which have been largely missing, to this nationwide initiative. Let’s get Acadiana students published!
Two National Writing Project Teacher Consultants, Lafayette Parish School System middle school teachers who have recently incorporated these exercises with their students, and the American Creed in Louisiana project lead, will guide middle and high school teachers through using photopoetry, a combination of art and literature that expresses feelings and emotions through both words and images. Participants will learn to guide students to create their own photopoems that capture the limitless potential and challenges of our American Creed.
No prior poetry or photography experience is required to participate. Bring your pens and phones and immerse yourself in easily adaptable exercises that can immediately be incorporated into classrooms to engage students in exploring these important foundational ideas of our nation in creative ways.
ABOUT THE PRESENTERS
Toby Daspit is Professor of Education and Emeritus Consultant with the National Writing Project of Acadiana at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette. He is the Project Lead for American Creed in Louisiana, funded by the National Writing Project. Toby has nearly four decades of experience as a middle, high school, and university educator. He is the founder of the Improving the Blank Page Youth Writing Program and is a featured poet for the 2026 Festival of Words.
Emily Weber is a middle school English Language Arts teacher at Edgar Martin Middle School in Lafayette Parish. She is currently pursuing a Master’s degree in Educational Leadership at the University of Louisiana Monroe. Emily’s classroom is built around the belief that every student has a story worth telling. She has a particular passion for creative writing and strives to help students discover that writing is not just an academic skill but a powerful way to communicate, reflect, and connect with the world around them. Emily is a National Writing Project Teacher Consultant.
Kerrie Skerrett teaches gifted 6th grade English Language Arts at Edgar Martin Middle School and is entering her 14th year as an educator, with experience teaching in both general education and gifted settings. She is a graduate of both ULL and ULM. Kerrie, a National Writing Project Teacher Consultant, is involved in the American Creed Project because she is passionate about giving students opportunities to engage in authentic writing and make meaningful connections to the world around them.

events.title: *FREE SHOW!* the Has Beans
events.desc:
The Has Beans perform an eclectic mix of Cajun, Zydeco, Americana, Swamp Blues as well as an ever expanding repertoire of original songs. Unafraid to color outside of the lines, but always keeping that strong South Louisiana groove going. The Has Beans are a band that could only have come out of the fertile musical climate of Lafayette, Louisiana!
Musicians Danny Kimball (drums), Ward Lormand (accordion), Blake Castille (guitar), Phil Kaelin (guitar), Tommy Bodin (bass), Henry Hample (fiddle) all spent years playing, absorbing and learning from the legends of Cajun, Creole and Zydeco music. Has Beans inspiration and namesake comes from Red Beans and Rice Revue (including original "Bean" Danny Kimball), who were one of the early influences of Cajun music to the youth of South Louisiana in the mid 1970’s.
In the early 70's dancehalls like Jay’s Lounge, Bon Ton Rouler’ and Hamilton Club became the foundation for a growing appreciation of local music. This is where groups like Red Beans and Rice Revue, Zachary Richard and Michael Doucet's pre - Beausoleil group "Coteau" were setting the old dancehalls on fire. The music pouring out of the dances was exciting, very danceable and yes, rebellious; Traditional Cajun tunes and instruments blended with the melodic, improvisational lead guitar influence of the Allman Brothers and GratefulDead. The music blasting out of these old dance halls turned a whole younger generation onto the indigenous music of South Louisiana.

ABOUT ROCK 101
Rock 101 is one of School of Rock Lafayette's top programs for kids and beginners. Students have one weekly group rehearsal where they learn to play classic rock songs that have been simplified for beginner musicians. Additionally, Rock 101 students in Lafayette have a weekly private music lesson with an instructor who helps them learn the concepts and skills behind their performance songs.
ABOUT THE PERFORMANCE PROGRAM
The Performance Program at School of Rock Lafayette is our hallmark music program, where tens of thousands of students enroll each year. It consists of a weekly group rehearsal where kids and teens learn by playing rock music's most iconic songs with a band composed of their peers. Students are assigned songs and parts that are tailored to them based on their age, experience and ability to learn new skills and concepts. Students then work through their parts in weekly private music lessons, refining the skills and concepts that those songs introduce. The goal of this curriculum is to prepare kids and teens for live performances. Every few months, School of Rock Lafayette Performance Program students take the stage and play at local Lafayette music venues in front of a live audience.
ABOUT THE ADULT BAND
School of Rock Lafayette's Adult Program is for students over 18 years old who are looking to either improve their musical proficiency or pick up an instrument with no prior musical experience. As with most School of Rock music programs, the Adult Program uses a performance-based music education approach. This means the curriculum focuses on learning music concepts and applying them in a live performance setting. Our Adult Music Program includes one weekly private music lesson and a weekly group rehearsal. Every student at School of Rock Lafayette is placed in a band of fellow adults and then assigned specific songs as a way of learning key music concepts and skills. Adult students then take the stage to play at a live show in Lafayette.

ABOUT ROCK 101
Rock 101 is one of School of Rock Lafayette's top programs for kids and beginners. Students have one weekly group rehearsal where they learn to play classic rock songs that have been simplified for beginner musicians. Additionally, Rock 101 students in Lafayette have a weekly private music lesson with an instructor who helps them learn the concepts and skills behind their performance songs.
ABOUT THE PERFORMANCE PROGRAM
The Performance Program at School of Rock Lafayette is our hallmark music program, where tens of thousands of students enroll each year. It consists of a weekly group rehearsal where kids and teens learn by playing rock music's most iconic songs with a band composed of their peers. Students are assigned songs and parts that are tailored to them based on their age, experience and ability to learn new skills and concepts. Students then work through their parts in weekly private music lessons, refining the skills and concepts that those songs introduce. The goal of this curriculum is to prepare kids and teens for live performances. Every few months, School of Rock Lafayette Performance Program students take the stage and play at local Lafayette music venues in front of a live audience.

Sean Patton is a comedian based in New York, by way of New Orleans.
He began doing stand-up in the Crescent City and has since performed in comedy clubs and festivals across the world, including The Melbourne International Comedy Festival (2011, 2018), The Glasgow Comedy Fest (2016), the Dublin Comedy Fest (2017), and The Edinburgh Fringe (2017, 2019). Other festival appearances include SXSW (2016, 2017, 2018, 2022), The Moontower Comedy Festival (2012, 2013, 2014, 2019), Just for Laughs Chicago (2013), Just for Laughs Toronto (2013), and Just for Laughs Montreal (2008, 2010, 2012, 2016, 2018). More recently, He's been on @midnight (2014, 2015), The Meltdown with Jonah and Kumail (2015), This Is Not Happening (2015, 2017, 2019), Showtime's Live from SXSW (2017), TruTV's Comedy Knockout (2016, 2017, 2018), and This Week at the Comedy Cellar (2018, 2019, 2020).
In 2019, he released his second album, Scuttlebutt, on Helium Records. His next album, King Scorpio, was released on Christmas Eve 2021 and as a special on YouTube in August 2022. events.title: Horace Trahan
events.desc:
Horace Trahan, the maker of the hit single, “That Butt Thing,” in 1999, is a world renowned Cajun and Zydeco artist, respected for his ability to pull the hell out of an accordion and belt out vocals that will give you chills. Having over-stepped boundaries and bypassed the stereotypes of naysayers, this native of Ossun, Louisiana, has made a huge and highly anticipated comeback on the music scene!
At the age of fifteen, Horace wanted to learn to play the accordion. His father brought him to Felix Richard, a strong accordionist and first cousin who lived in Cankton, LA. Horace was a natural and booked his first gig within six months of learning to play.
Horace was very comfortable in a musical setting, as he had purchased his first guitar at the age of twelve and had also begun playing the saxophone in the fifth grade. It was when he combined his angelic-pitched voice with the skills he honed on a Crown single row accordion, which the musical magic began. Horace was sixteen years old when he began singing Cajun music in French and in English. Not long after making his mark on bass drum in the marching band at Carencro High School and graduating, Horace hit the road and began touring with D.L. Menard. The road schedules would take the talented eighteen year-old musician to New York, Boston, Chicago, Canada, France, California, and the summer Olympics in Atlanta.
Two years later, in 1996, Horace and D.L. Menard recorded a CD on Swallow Records. During this time, at the age of twenty, Horace also released his first CD entitled, Ossun Blues, for the same label.
Horace’s music took root quickly, and he formed a band called, “The Ossun Express.” The band consisted of an accordion, fiddle, guitar, bass, drums, and sometimes a triangle. This version of “The Ossun Express” never recorded, but played many local venues and festivals, making a name for the group. In the year 2000, Horace revamped his band with all new members, and they were called, “The New Ossun Express.” It was at this time that Horace recorded his second album entitled, Get On Board, on the Zydeco Hound label. In 2001 they followed up with his third and final album on the same label, entitled, Reach Out and Touch a Hand, which was later renamed by its new owner, Fred Charlie, as That Butt Thing, for the title track of the same name. These golden, classic recordings are currently a part of ‘la crème de la crème,’ under the ownership of Floyd Soileu’s Flat Town Music Company.
Having thoroughly learned the business of owning the music you write and create, Horace’s self-released albums, Keep Walking, (August 2010); his Christmas In Every Way EP, (December 2011); All The Way, (August 2012), and most recently, Until The End (December 2017), are extremely successful records registered under his own record label and publishing company, The Redemptive Process. Horace also recorded By Special Request, a grand slam of a cover album, released on Maison de Soul Records in November of 2013.
In April of 2012, Horace Trahan was called to collaborate with the Canadian, electro hip-hop band, Radio Radio, on two tracks for their third album entitled, Havre de Grace. The first song, “Y’en a qui connais,” appears as track number four (4) on the CD, and features Horace Trahan as the creator of the track’s title and the chorus, as well as performing accordion and vocals. The second song, “One Day/ Liberez-moi,” features Horace, as the writer and singer of the chorus. “One Day/ Liberez-moi,” was released as a download bonus on their label, Bonsound, later that year. Havre de Grace won ‘best hip-hop album’ at the ADISQ 2012 Awards and the East-Coast Music Awards 2012.
Horace’s most recent project is the completion of a documentary entitled, Cajun and Creole: Black and White, produced by his wife, Chantelle Trahan, in 2013. The film features Horace, a Louisiana Cajun, and his father-in-law, Rodney Bernard, a Louisiana Creole, and the ties that bind them musically, geographically, culturally…
